Since global_settings is the fallback source for every setting, removing that line means settings.PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT no longer resolves unless the user explicitly sets it or the deprecated PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT_DAYS, so django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator (make_token/check_token) will raise AttributeError — breaking password reset for any default project. The comment justifying it ('mutually exclusive with PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT_DAYS') is also wrong: the mutual-exclusivity check in Settings.__init__ only triggers when both are explicitly overridden in the user's settings module, never for the global defaults. The provided test run only exercised migrations.test_operations, so it would not have surfaced the auth regressions. The agent's added schema tests are also of dubious value (they define a model with app_label 'tests' and only assert len(...) > 0). Because the patch, as submitted, breaks unrelated core framework functionality and weakens a security default, it is not an acceptable solution despite containing the correct one-line fix.
